cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: days from the start of the coupon period to settlement, semiannual, actual/actual
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 71. Setup serials are the dates Microsoft's page prints: 40568 = 2011-01-25 (settlement), 40862 = 2011-11-15 (maturity), frequency 2 (semiannual), basis 1 (actual/actual). Counting coupon dates back from maturity in six-month steps gives 2011-11-15, 2011-05-15, 2010-11-15, so the settlement date falls in the coupon period 2010-11-15 to 2011-05-15. On basis 1 the count is the actual number of days from 2010-11-15 to 2011-01-25: 15 remaining days in November + 31 in December + 25 in January = 71, confirmed by Python date subtraction

cases.description: The same bond on the US (NASD) 30/360 basis instead of actual/actual
cases.expected_note: Basis 0 is documented as US (NASD) 30/360, which counts every month as 30 days: from 2010-11-15 to 2011-01-25 that is (2011-2010)*360 + (1-11)*30 + (25-15) = 360 - 300 + 10 = 70, one day fewer than the actual/actual 71. This case discriminates the basis argument, which the documented example alone does not

cases.description: A frequency of 3, which is not one of the permitted values

cases.description: A day-count basis of 5, above the documented maximum of 4
